name: demo
about: An invented studio that makes short, calm films from data. It exists so Slate's demo film, its tests and anyone trying Slate have a complete, neutral brand to work with. It is not a real company.

ownership.notes: Slate's own neutral pack. It lives in Slate's repo, so commands never change it: to onboard something from it, copy it into your store with `slate brand init <name> --from-pack demo`.

palette.notes: Warm stone neutrals, one clay accent, a deep harbour slate for inverse surfaces. Clay is the only colour that carries meaning: the line, the accent, the mark's keystone.

contrast_pairs.where: large numerals and headlines in clay

families.licence: SIL Open Font License 1.1 (an open font, served by Google Fonts)
SIL Open Font License 1.1 (an open font, served by Google Fonts)

type.notes: One open family in two weights, tabular figures on every number. The display role is the same family at 700, so After Effects gets its own PostScript name for headings.

mark.notes: Three tiles and a round keystone, drawn for the demo. The tiles build left to right; the clay keystone drops in last and lands.

motif.notes: The mark's four parts as a rig, for the rare film where the mark acts. It moves as one piece at small sizes and never loops except to breathe.

look.notes: The kit's flat look in the studio's stone and clay. A real brand's look comes from its own design language during onboarding, never from this pack.

arrive.job: everything that enters: type, cards, UI, count-ups, draw-ons
arrive.lineage: drawn for the demo pack: a firm, soft landing that settles early (not measured from any product)

carry.job: rest-to-rest moves of things already on screen, and the camera
carry.lineage: drawn for the demo pack: a symmetric in-out that starts and ends at rest

switch.job: state changes: a chip flips, a check lands, a toggle commits
switch.lineage: drawn for the demo pack: a held breath, then a quick commit

depart.lineage: drawn for the demo pack: gathers speed and leaves without slamming

make-room.job: short re-layouts: a line pushes a block, a list re-sorts
make-room.lineage: drawn for the demo pack: a small, even lift

settle.lineage: the kit's zero-bounce spring, a little softer: a settle, never a bounce

linear.job: only things that show time: progress, a playhead, a constant spin

tick.use: chip flips, checks, a dot lighting

base.use: standard entrances: a line of type, a card

signature.use: the logo build and the act's one signature moment

overshoot.notes: Nothing bounces. A container that grows uses settle, which lands without passing its target.

signature.name: keystone build
signature.what: the mark builds tile by tile, left to right, and its clay keystone drops in last and lands
signature.sound: one hollow wood knock as the keystone lands, with a small felt note under it

banned.why: entrances start from at least 85% of their size
the studio's motion is calm; settle lands without passing its target
pieces are carried from beat to beat
banned.exception: a cut hidden inside a fast move's blur

banned.why: every visible move uses one of the named eases

motion.notes: Drawn for the demo pack as a sound, neutral law to start from. A real brand's law is measured from its own product and two or three reference films during onboarding.

voice.notes: A public ElevenLabs library voice (the one its own API examples use), so the demo can be voiced for real with --live. Check it's still in the library before a live run: slate voice cast --brand demo --voices JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb. model null means the registry's current best, pinned per film.

motif.figure: three rising notes (the first, third and fifth of the key) as the keystone lands

palette.source: seeded from proof 2's taste as a starting point: pads, small felt notes, hollow wood clicks, no chimes

sound.notes: Proof 2's taste as the starting point: soft pads, small felt notes and hollow wood clicks and knocks, one deliberate sound per kind of interaction, every sound on its beat, and never a chime. A real brand gets its own palette during onboarding.

sources.note: The studio is invented for Slate's demo, so its only source is this pack.

claim_authority.name: Demo Owner
claim_authority.note: A placeholder. A real brand names a real person, and for a brand the owner doesn't own, a person at that organisation.

approved_claims.text: Demo Studio makes short films from data.
Every film is checked before it ships.

never_claim.text: Demo Studio is a real company
Demo Studio has customers or testimonials
never_claim.why: an invented studio has no customers, and invented quotes are never shown as real

truth.notes: Everything here is invented and labelled as such. It gives the story gates a complete truth pack to check a demo script against.

grounding.notes: The demo has no brand kits. A real brand's ElevenLabs and Higgsfield brand-kit ids go here, so every generation is grounded in the brand.

truth.note: Unapproved by design: the demo is a neutral stand-in, and supervised demo films don't need it.

look_motion.note: Unapproved by design: a real brand approves a moving 10–15 second look-and-motion test with sound.

voice.note: Unapproved by design: a real brand approves a take with its model, settings and seed.

sound.note: Unapproved by design: a real brand approves a 10–20 second sound proof with its levels measured against the voice.
